name: Pentlatch
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Andreatta, Mat, Jessie Recalma & Suzanne Urbanczyk. 2023. Boas and the Babblefish (Part I): Turning pentl'ach Vowels into Consonants. Papers for ICSNL 58 (Reisinger et al. eds.), pp. 1-9. Vancouver: UBCWPL.
sources.note: Only transcriptional: p.7 'We have also found the accent mark used to indicate primary stress.' and p.7 '..the accent mark is to be interpreted as an indicator of stress, rather than a glottal stop.' Boas's <V'V> = V + syllable-final glottal stop. No statement of where stress falls.

Paper presented at the 21st Conference on American Indian Languages (American Anthropological Association). Ms. in M. Dale Kinkade Papers, University of Washington Libraries Special Collections, Accession 5108-005, Series 1 (Research Files), Box 1, folder 'Pentlatch: Transcription Practices' (undated).

sources.access_detail: in print; a research-library copy was located; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.note: By title the one work devoted to interpreting Boas's 1886 Pentlatch diacritics (accent mark, apostrophe, macron/breve), hence the likeliest first-hand statement of what the accent mark encodes (primary stress) and whether any pitch notation exists; no tone claim expected for a Central Salish language. Unpublished; only the archival folder was located.
